[Rating: 2/10] Not good. It reminds me a lot of 7 Wonders: Architects with its draw-discard. I'm not sure I fully grokked this one, however I find the whole thing really dull and abstracted. I'd rather play 7 Wonders, and that is saying a lot.

[Rating: 2/10] I didn't think it was possible to make the 7 Wonders formula [i]less [/i] interesting. Track-nudging, set collection, and point conversion so lifeless and disenchanting as to almost feel like a satire of modern euro design.

[Rating: 2/10] J'ai rarement vu un jeu aussi inintéressant. Aucun thème, choix limité, un pur jeu d'optimisation sans saveur, un tableau excel.  J'étais en bonne compagnie avec mes amis, alors j'ai passé un bon moment car j'aime jouer autour d'une table, mais le jeu, lui...

[Rating: 2/10] Card drafting, point scoring. Both theme and mechanic not my type. Other better drafting games.

[Rating: 3/10] Way too many opportunities for analysis paralysis. The rule about putting cards on top of other cards and later choosing from those cards is especially terrible, as it adds the need to memorize the card effects and their position in relation to turn order. Very bad.  Rewards are given in steps, which are quite far apart - as a result meticulous planning is necessary, leading to more analysis. Thematically, the game could be anything. Components are OK-ish, with some unfortunate choices (the +10 tokens are hard to see, player boards are on the fiddly side of things, tokens are extremely fiddly)

[Rating: 3/10] Decent draft but when we calculated scores at the end I realized I didn't know what a single one of the pictures on my cards were-boring and I can't remember a single meaningful thing this game did different than other drafts

[Rating: 3/10] Take everything redeemable about 7 Wonders and gut it, slather with a coat of new-hotness, and bill it as the 7-Wonders-Killer. Only it’s not. And I actively dislike 7 Wonders.

[Rating: 3/10] Hadara was 60 minutes of heads down optimization. There is no interaction or reason to look at anything but your own tableau and the cards that are available for purchase. I did not have a bad time with it, but there was nothing special about the game. Actually, there is something special and that is the cover art. It's wonderfully goofy and I love that! I cannot believe that it is getting replaced by some bland collage in the newer printings. Bummer. At least, presentation and gameplay will be on the same level in the future.

[Rating: 3/10] "What if we added an economy board to 7 Wonders and made the game three times longer?" asked no one, ever.

[Rating: 3/10] A kind of euro thematic game of civilizations that does not go anywhere. It fails for the theme and it fails for the mechanics. There are much better options out there.

[Rating: 3/10] A Crown of Emara parádés Schwertől, bármikor előveszem, mert bár nincs benne interakció, de a rondel nekem elviszi a hátán. Ez meg nekem lelketlen, kőeurósként is száraz, nulla interakció van benne... Nem én vagyok a célközönség. Jó játék annak, aki szeret magában molyolni, de én nem ez vagyok. Ritkán unatkozok játékokban, de itt az volt...

[Rating: 3/10] 2023-06-17 (1 play at 4 on BGA): I thought I wanted a simpler 7 Wonders, but maybe I just don't want to play 7 Wonders. This actually feels even less thematic, though, which might be the bigger problem for me.   I think there's probably a stimulating maths puzzle here with tough choices, but it has fewer imaginative hooks, lower interaction, and even less intuitive scoring than the game it streamlines. I'm not going to be returning to assess the quality of this product. I suspect it has value. It's not for me.
